arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Geyser argued the statute covers lost income and necessary expenses.
Mr. Huston argued the statute enables recovery for any investigation participation.
Justice Breyer posed a hypothetical about a private investigator hired by a company.
Justice Roberts asked if government-requested private investigations would be covered.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks if the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act covers private investigation costs. the side that brought the case Lagos seeks recovery for these expenses. The United States opposes this interpretation. The Court must define the scope of covered expenses.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Lagos wants the Court to allow recovery of private investigation costs.
The United States wants the Court to limit restitution to government investigation costs.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Lagos argues the statute covers all necessary expenses during any investigation.
The United States argues the statute only covers government-led investigations.
